subject: zoology
question_text: What do you mean by parasitic castration? Give one example.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.58, VSAQ 133). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Degeneration of the gonads of the host caused by
the presence of a parasite is called parasitic
The host can no longer breed.
steps.why: The definition names the organ that is damaged, the gonad, and the cause, the parasite — and the loss of breeding is what makes it 'castration'.
common_mistakes: Writing that the parasite eats the host. The damage is to the gonads only.
Leaving out the word gonads and writing 'reproductive organs are affected'. Use the syllabus word.
steps.memory_tip: Castration means the gonad stops working; here a parasite, not surgery, causes it.
steps.margin_note: One sentence naming the gonads and the parasite. A second short line on breeding is enough.

steps.label: Example
lines: Sacculina is a crustacean parasite of crabs.
Its presence causes the ovaries of the crab to
degenerate, so the crab cannot breed.
steps.why: The example is marked as a pair — the parasite and the host it castrates — because either name alone does not show the effect.
common_mistakes: Naming Sacculina without naming the crab.
Writing that Sacculina kills the crab. The crab lives on; only the gonads degenerate.
steps.memory_tip: Sacculina and crab: the parasite stays, the crab's ovaries go.
steps.margin_note: Name both, then one line on what degenerates. Two lines.

insider_note: Both marks are name-bound: the definition must contain the word gonads and the example must contain both Sacculina and crab.
